mcqs.question: Which four volumes does the review list as the standard static lung volumes?

options.A: Tidal, inspiratory reserve, expiratory reserve, and residual volume
options.B: FEV1, peak flow, DLCO, and FVC only
options.D: Inspiratory capacity is a volume rather than a capacity in this sentence
options.E: The review does not name them

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Tidal, inspiratory reserve, expiratory reserve, and residual volume
mcqs.explanation: The static volumes named are tidal, inspiratory reserve, expiratory reserve, and residual volume. The capacities are listed separately.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The static lung volumes/capacities are further subdivided into four standard volumes (tidal, inspiratory reserve, expiratory reserve, and residual volumes) and four standard capacities (inspiratory, functional residual, vital and total lung capacities).

mcqs.question: Why can residual volume, FRC, and total lung capacity not be measured with a simple spirometer?

options.A: Residual volume is part of both FRC and TLC, so those capacities include gas that a spirometer does not measure
options.C: Residual volume is the same as vital capacity
options.D: The review says a spirometer is sufficient for all static volumes
options.E: FRC is an exhaled volume only

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Residual volume is part of both FRC and TLC, so those capacities include gas that a spirometer does not measure
mcqs.explanation: RV is part of FRC and of TLC, so those capacities are impossible to measure through simple spirometers.

sourceRefs.excerpt: RV constitutes part of FRC as well as TLC and, therefore, these capacities are impossible to measure through simple spirometers.

mcqs.question: Which methods does the review name for measuring RV, FRC, and TLC?

options.A: Radiology, body plethysmography, or dilution methods such as helium dilution and nitrogen washout

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Radiology, body plethysmography, or dilution methods such as helium dilution and nitrogen washout
mcqs.explanation: Measurement is based on radiological, plethysmographic, or dilutional techniques, including helium dilution and nitrogen washout.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The procedures used for measurement of RV, FRC and TLC are based on radiological, plethysmographic or dilutional techniques (helium dilution and nitrogen washout methods) [4].

mcqs.question: For which ventilatory defects does the review say static lung volumes are important?

options.C: Neither; only the flow-volume loop matters

mcqs.explanation: Static lung volumes are equally important for evaluation of obstructive as well as restrictive ventilatory defects. Dynamic volumes are described as essential for obstructive disease.

sourceRefs.excerpt: static lung volumes are equally important for evaluation of obstructive as well as restrictive ventilatory defects.

mcqs.question: In obstruction, air trapping correlates positively with which volumes?

options.A: RV, FRC, TLC, and the RV/TLC ratio
options.E: The review says air trapping lowers RV

mcqs.correctAnswerText: RV, FRC, TLC, and the RV/TLC ratio
mcqs.explanation: Air trapping correlates positively with RV, FRC, TLC, and RV/TLC, and negatively with VC, IC, and IC/TLC.

sourceRefs.excerpt: air trapping in obstructive ventilatory defects correlates positively with RV, FRC, TLC and RV/TLC, but negatively with VC, IC and IC/TLC.
